explanation: Supergroup Amoebozoa (Amoebazoa) includes protozoans that move using pseudopods (false-feet). Amoeboids ingest food via phagocytosis using their pseudopods and digest it within food vacuoles. One infectious amoeboid species causes dysentery. Slime molds, also in this supergroup, are decomposers that feed on dead plant material. They are not fungi because they lack cell walls and possess flagella during a portion of their life cycle. A plasmodial slime mold acts as a slug-like organism that consumes decaying matter on the forest floor. Individual amoeboid cells aggregate to form a pseudoplasmodium, which develops a sporangium and spores during unfavorable conditions, germinating when conditions improve.

questions.q: Why are slime molds not classified as fungi?
opts: They lack cell walls and have flagella for a portion of their life.
They contain a porous silica shell.

questions.q: What happens when conditions are not favorable for a slime mold?
opts: It undergoes conjugation via a sex pilus.
It develops a sporangium and spores.
It forms an envelope containing lipids.
